content: When the Master governs, the people are hardly aware that he exists. When his work is done, his aim fulfilled, they will say: 'We did it ourselves.'
author: Lao Tzu
story:
Serving as royal archivist during the moral disintegration of the Eastern Zhou Dynasty, Lao Tzu grew disillusioned with political intrigue and artificial societal rituals. Legend tells that before vanishing into the western wilderness atop a water buffalo, the border guard Yinxi persuaded him to record the timeless paradoxes of nature, effortless action (Wu Wei), and yielding strength.

This timeless reminder speaks to the universal struggle to balance inner truth with outer demands. Lao Tzu understood that the measure of a meaningful life is not external approval, but the quiet integrity with which we meet each day's encounters.
reflectionPrompt: What would change in your daily outlook if you truly lived by this perspective?
